system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring

ATOM KGBDP-C09-S2-03 (S2): Unsupervised NILM techniques are widely applied because labeled data are unavailable for the houses in which services will be installed; examples include clustering and histogram analysis before conditional random fields, adaptation over unlabeled data, and single-channel source separation via Non Negative Matrix Factorization and Separation Via Tensor and Matrix Factorization.

EVIDENCE:
[KGBDP-p0174-s13] The main cause of this is the fact that labeled data for the houses in which services are going to be installed are not available, as already discussed.
[KGBDP-p0174-s14] Therefore, many authors choose to use unsupervised learning techniques instead of improving generalization on the supervised ones.
[KGBDP-p0174-s15] Examples of these attempts are shown in [194] where clusterization and histogram analysis has been employed before using the conditional random fields approach, in [344] where adaptation over unlabeled data has been carried out in order to improve performance on the gaining houses, and in [136] where disaggregation was described as a single-channel source separation problem and Non Negative Matrix Factorization and Separation Via Tensor and Matrix Factorization were used.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Combines the reason for unsupervised learning with several independently assessable method examples. / Joins the rationale for unsupervised NILM with three separate examples of specific methods from individual studies.
- L1_ONLY: revise — Retain the missing-label motivation; remove the catalogue of separate technical methods and their processing relationships. / The list of specific multi-stage setups from three individual papers adds excessive recall load beyond the core fact of why unsupervised methods are used.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT: hold — The specific pipeline examples (e.g., clustering and histogram analysis before CRFs) reflect specific cited papers [194, 344, 136] rather than general truths.

Also removed the unsupported 'widely applied' wording, using the evidence's 'many authors'."}
